original: Oke so the header Q: do like that, quote it, so it's not blend the main context
corrected: OK, so do the same for the `Q:` header — quote it too, so it doesn't blend into the main content.

fixes.body: "Oke" → "OK" (or "Okay")
"it's not blend" → "it doesn't blend" — `blend` is a full verb here, so the negative takes `does`, not `is`
"blend the main context" → "blend into the main content" — `blend` needs the preposition `into`; and `content` is the text itself, while `context` is the situation around it

original: If you do that, maybe you can call fail if my net work error? so if word is easy for you, i permit you can write with your trainning data, just do word if not in your training data, because i know that, you are perfect in english, ipa call is redundant in most case
corrected: *If you do that, the call might fail whenever my network is down. So for easy words, I'll let you write the IPA from your training data — only look one up if it's not in there. I know your English is excellent, so the IPA lookup is redundant in most cases.*

fixes.body: "net work" → "network" · "trainning" → "training"
"maybe you can call fail" → "the call might fail" — `fail` is the main verb here, so it needs its own subject; `you can call fail` stacks three verbs with no subject for the last one
"i permit you can write" → "I'll let you write" — `let` takes a bare verb (`let you write`); `permit` is formal and needs `to` (`permit you to write`)
"if word is easy" → "if a word is easy" — a singular countable noun can't stand alone

original: No i want it in above Learn something new, and dont need word vocab in learning something new, let it like it be (just additional to learn, not decribe that, it do not have any value
corrected: *No — I want it **above** "Learn something new". And don't gloss the words inside that block; leave it as it is. It's just an extra thing to read, not material to study — that has no value.*

fixes.body: "i want it in above" → "I want it above" — `above` is already a preposition, so `in` is one too many
"it do not have" → "it doesn't have" — third person singular takes `does`
"let it like it be" → "leave it as it is" — that's the fixed English phrase
"decribe" → "describe"

original:
i want that vocabulary have example below
  ▎ - bulk /bʌlk/ (n) — the largest part of something, by volume
  ▎ - bare /ber/ (adj) — with nothing in it; empty of content
  ▎ - verbatim /vɚˈbeɪ.t̬əm/ (adv) — copied word for word, with no change
  ▎ - non-compliant /ˌnɑːn.kəmˈplaɪ.ənt/ (adj) — not following a rule it is supposed to follow
corrected: I want each vocabulary entry to have an example below it.

fixes.body: "want that vocabulary have" → "want each entry to have" — after *want*, English uses *want + object + to + verb*, never *want that…*
